newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: CRICKET-Leave tight catches for 3rd umpire-Rixon.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-Leave tight catches for 3rd umpire-Rixon.

text.p: CHRISTCHURCH, Feb 17 - Television replays could be used for tight catching appeals in test cricket, according to New Zealand coach Steve Rixon.
Rixon was speaking after New Zealand opener Bryan Young had stood his ground after being given out during the third test against England at Lancaster Park yesterday.
Australian umpire Darrell Hair gave Young out after he was caught at silly mid off by Nick Knight off left-arm spinner Phil Tufnell for 49 in New Zealand's second innings.
Young indicated he felt the ball had bounced on the ground before Knight claimed the catch. He said so as well, and television replays appeared to back his view.
Hair then had a lengthy discussion with fellow umpire Steve Dunne before again signalling Young was out.
Last night match referee Peter Burge of Australia decided to take no action against Young, stating he believed Young hadn't seen Hair give him out initially.
"Given his unblemished record, I have decided to take no further action," Burge said in a statement.
Rixon said incidents such as Young's dismissal supported a case for enlarging the role of the third umpire.
At present the third official judges tight run out and stumping decisions, after one of the umpires signals for his assistance.
"I don't want to make robots out of umpires," Rixon said.
"They've got a job to do and it was obviously a very difficult decision.
"But at the end of the day, if you're taking stumpings and run outs on board for the close ones, for something like that (Young's dismissal), maybe it's best that they do view it."
